title: Pricing by hours per project for bond and end-of-lease cleaning
audience: Owners and crew leads of bond and end-of-lease cleaning businesses who quote move-out cleans and need a price that covers cost and earns a margin.
learningOutcomes: Calculate a cost per productive hour from the owner's own figures
Estimate project hours, including set-up, travel and checking time
Build a quote from hours, a rate and a margin, and state its basis and exclusions

instruction.heading: Why hours are the starting unit for a move-out
instruction.body: A move-out clean is mostly time: the crew on site, the trip, set-up and a checking pass against the agent's list. Start from hours, so each quote shows its cost and the effect of an added item such as the oven or windows. The research has no bond-specific cost data. The only move-out table it contains is short-stay fee data from Beyond Pricing (28 October 2026), which is used here as a proxy only.

instruction.heading: Build the cost per productive hour
instruction.body: Divide the year's total business costs by chargeable hours. Include wages with on-costs where you employ staff, plus vehicle running costs, chemicals, equipment, insurance and admin. Business.gov.au says on-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure (1 October 2026). Xero Australia advises dividing by billable hours, not total hours (3 September 2026). Jobber's cleaning guide says cleaners often undercount on-costs, which it puts at 25 to 40 per cent of wages; it is US-leaning, so it is not an Australian rate.

instruction.heading: Estimate the hours for each move-out
instruction.body: Break the job into rooms and items: kitchen, bathrooms, oven, fridge, cupboards, windows and floors. Time each at a standard speed from past move-outs, and add set-up, pack-down, travel and a checking pass as named lines. Add a set allowance for delays such as late access or unfinished packing. Xero Australia suggests 10 to 20 per cent for unexpected work; that is the source's own range, not a bond benchmark.

instruction.heading: Turn hours into a price, then test it against the proxy
instruction.body: Multiply crew hours by the cost per productive hour, then add a margin that reflects the risk in the job, such as a dirty condition or a tight handover. Compare the total with the proxy band of $160 to $220 for a two-bedroom move-out. That band is for short-stay fees and is not a bond price. If your cost-based price is above it, show the scope the band leaves out. Do not cut the cost to meet the band.

instruction.heading: Keep the quote honest
instruction.body: The quote states the agent's list or your scope, the hours basis, exclusions (for example, windows or carpets if not included), what the agent or tenant must provide (access, keys, power and water on) and the validity date. Business Queensland suggests charging unplanned extra costs at cost plus a stated percentage; one source suggests 15 per cent, which is a suggestion, not a benchmark (16 November 2022).

procedure: Get the agent's cleaning list and the entry condition report, if they exist.
Gather the year's total costs and chargeable hours for the same period, with a source for each figure.
Divide costs by chargeable hours and date the cost per productive hour.
Estimate each room and item as a range, using timed past move-outs.
Add set-up, pack-down, travel and checking as named lines.
Multiply crew hours by the cost per productive hour, add the margin, then compare with the proxy band.
Write the quote with scope, hours basis, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
Record actual hours for each move-out and review the variance monthly.

workedExamples.situation: [ILLUSTRATIVE] A Melbourne cleaner quotes a move-out for a two-bedroom apartment. Estimate: 4.5 hours on site for the agent's list, 0.5 hours set-up and pack-down, 0.75 hours travel and 0.75 hours checking, which is 6.5 crew-hours. Cost per productive hour is $55 (illustrative; not sourced). Target margin is 25 per cent of price (illustrative).
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the cost and the price, and how does the price compare with the proxy band?
workedExamples.reasoning: The cost is 6.5 x $55, which is $357.50 (illustrative). A 25 per cent margin on price means the price is the cost divided by 0.75, which is $476.67 (CALC). The Beyond Pricing move-out band for a two-bedroom home is $160 to $220 (vendor, 28 October 2026). That band is short-stay fee data, so the difference is a reason to test the hours and the scope, not a finding about bond prices. The cleaner checks that 4.5 on-site hours is realistic and shows the list the price covers. Floor check: the Cleaning Services Award Level 1 adult minimum of $25.85 an hour, with 25 per cent casual loading, is $32.31 an hour (Fair Work Commission; 1 July 2025 variation). Six and a half hours at that floor is $210.02 before on-costs, so the floor is not the cost per hour.

equipmentAndPpe: Time log for each job, with estimated and actual columns
Measuring tape or laser measure for area estimates

commonErrors.error: Pricing from the hourly wage alone.
commonErrors.prevention: Include on-costs, vehicle, chemicals, equipment, insurance and admin in the cost per productive hour.

commonErrors.error: Using the short-stay fee table as a bond price.
commonErrors.prevention: Label it as a proxy. Bond-specific pricing was not found in the research.

commonErrors.error: Quoting a move-out with no list and no exclusions.
commonErrors.prevention: Attach the agent's list, name the exclusions and state what the agent or tenant must provide.

commonErrors.error: Cutting the cost per hour to meet a proxy band.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the hours and the scope first. Show what the band leaves out.

commonErrors.error: Never comparing estimated and actual hours.
commonErrors.prevention: Record actual hours for each move-out and review the variance every month.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Pricing guidance only. The Australian Consumer Law applies to price statements, and the ACCC says misleading statements about prices are prohibited (ACCC, 15 July 2026). State rules differ, so check your state's fair trading rules.

Where you employ cleaners, the Cleaning Services Award (MA000022) may set their minimum rates. The Level 1 adult minimum was $25.85 an hour, with a 25 per cent casual loading, from 1 July 2025. The 2026-27 rates were not checked.
Victorian renting rules affect whether an agent can require a professional clean (Consumer Affairs Victoria, 14 October 2026). They do not set prices. Other states' rules were not checked.

qualityStandard: Each quote shows scope, hours or price basis, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
The cost per productive hour is calculated from the owner's own records and dated.
Actual hours are recorded for at least the first ten jobs of each type and compared with the estimate.
No quote is issued without a margin decision and a minimum-charge check.
documentationEvidence: Cost per productive hour worksheet, dated, with the source of each figure
Quote showing scope, hours basis, exclusions and validity
Job time log with estimated and actual hours
summary: Start every move-out quote from measured hours and a cost per chargeable hour.
Name the list, travel, set-up and checking, and state the exclusions and access in writing.
Gaps: bond-specific cost data, agent margin expectations and 2026-27 award rates were not sourced. The move-out band is a proxy.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which costs belong in the cost per productive hour for a move-out crew?
options: Only the hourly wage of the lowest-paid worker
Wages with on-costs, vehicle, chemicals, equipment, insurance and admin, divided by chargeable hours
The price the agent pays, plus any deposit taken
The rate a short-stay competitor advertises

knowledgeChecks.question: A move-out is estimated at 6 crew-hours and takes 8. What should you do?
options: Record the actual hours, find the cause, and adjust the estimate and future quotes
Leave the estimate as it is, because the agent has paid
Cut the crew's breaks on the next job
Raise the price for this agent only and change nothing else

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does a bond quote need a stated list and exclusions?
options: To make the quote longer for the agent to read
To show what the price covers, so extra items can be priced and disputes reduced
To hide the margin from the agent
To lower the agent's expectations of the clean

sourceReferences: business.gov.au, 'Choose a pricing strategy', https://business.gov.au/products-and-services/choose-a-pricing-strategy, page metadata dated 1 October 2026. Supports: on-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure.

Xero Australia, 'How to price services', https://www.xero.com/au/guides/how-to-price-services/, dated 3 September 2026. Supports: divide by billable hours, not total hours; add a set allowance for delays; the guide's 10 to 20 per cent range for unexpected work is the source's own figure.

Jobber Academy, 'How Much to Charge for House Cleaning', https://getjobber.com/academy/cleaning/how-much-to-charge-for-house-cleaning/, 31 March 2026 (first published June 2023). US-leaning source. Supports: cleaners often undercount on-costs such as payroll tax, workers' compensation and unpaid travel, which the source puts at 25 to 40 per cent of wages; a profit factor on cost; annual price reviews; a flat or minimum-hours charge for short cleaning jobs.

Beyond Pricing, 'Short-term rental cleaning fees (Australia)', https://beyondpricing.com/au/blog/how-much-should-you-charge-for-cleaning-fees-in-your-australian-holiday-rental, dated 28 October 2026. Vendor source; short-stay fee data. Supports: per-turnover bands by property size; move-in and move-out bands by bedroom count; a $120 per-turnover illustration; city labour benchmarks; fixed rates suit smaller properties and hourly rates suit larger or luxury homes.

ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, page last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading statements about prices are prohibited.

Fair Work Commission, Cleaning Services Award (MA000022), https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000022.html, variation effective 1 July 2025. Supports: Level 1 adult minimum hourly rate of $25.85 and a 25 per cent casual loading. The 1 July 2026 position was not checked.

Consumer Affairs Victoria, 'Condition reports', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/housing/renting/rent-bond-bills-and-condition-reports/condition-reports, last updated 14 October 2026. Victoria. Supports: for agreements from 29 March 2021 a provider cannot ask renters to get professional cleaning unless the property must be returned to its starting state or needs professional cleaning; exit condition report within 10 days; renter present or given a reasonable opportunity; evidence at least 3 business days before a claim.

Business Queensland, 'Preparing a business quote: tips', https://www.business.qld.gov.au/running-business/marketing-sales/sales/preparing-quote/tips, last updated 16 November 2022. Queensland. Supports: list add-ons and alternatives on the quote; charge extra costs at cost plus a stated percentage (the source suggests 15 per cent, which is not a benchmark); follow up 7 to 14 days after the quote; confirm scope, capacity and deadline before quoting.
Notes: $55 an hour, the hours and the 25 per cent margin are illustrative and not sourced. The $160 to $220 band is a proxy from short-stay fee data. The Victorian rule is Victoria only.
